comparison: Perfect agreement on ATF6α trafficking and processing claims (C61-C67). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing using confocal microscopy, immunoblotting, and redox analysis. OpenEval provides more technical detail about the reporter systems, while peer reviewers emphasize the overall convincing nature of the evidence package.

Perfect agreement on CRT-ATF6α direct interaction claims (C6-C7, C68-C72). Both accept the BLI and co-IP evidence as convincing. OpenEval discusses the physiological relevance of the KD value and dual binding modes, while peer reviewers emphasize this as providing 'new mechanistic insight' without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on dual reporter system validation (C37-C44). Both evaluations confirm the reporter system is specific and functional. OpenEval details the technical validation showing ATF6α knockout effects and minimal perturbation of endogenous pathways, while peer reviewers praise the 'innovative experimental design.'

Perfect agreement on CNX and ERp18 negative controls (C58, C86). Both evaluations accept these as demonstrating CRT specificity. OpenEval explicitly notes cell-type-specific differences compared to other systems, while peer reviewers accept these as supporting robustness of CRT findings.

Strong agreement on FURIN findings (C45-C50, C87-C88). Both accept that FURIN acts indirectly on ATF6α activation. OpenEval notes the limitation that in vitro cleavage failed, restricting mechanistic understanding, while peer reviewers accept this as appropriately supported secondary finding from the screen.

Strong agreement on IRE1 pathway effects and feedback loop (C8-C9, C55, C80-C84). Both find evidence convincing for reduced IRE1 activity in CRT-depleted cells. OpenEval notes the mechanism remains indirect, while peer reviewers emphasize this as 'new mechanistic insight' into ATF6-IRE1 crosstalk. Peer review includes additional claims C59-C60 about ATF6α inactivation rescue.

Strong agreement on CRT depletion phenotype (C3-C5, C54-C57). Both evaluations support the finding that CRT depletion leads to constitutive ATF6α activation. OpenEval covers broader screen identification claims (C2, C52-C53, C59-C60) while peer review focuses on validation experiments. Both describe evidence as convincing.

Partial agreement on CRT mutant rescue experiments (C76-C79). Both support the functional evidence for glycan binding role. OpenEval expresses concern about CRTY92A,W244A protein integrity (C77) limiting conclusions about Erp57 co-chaperone role, while peer reviewers accepted these structure-function studies without critique. OpenEval also addresses mechanistic interpretation claims (C92, C95) not included in peer R6.

Partial agreement on ATF6α knock-in rescue experiments (C73-C75). Both support that N-glycosylation and disulfide bonds are required for ATF6α function. OpenEval notes lower ΔGly expression complicates interpretation, while peer reviewers accepted findings without critique. Peer R6 also includes CRT mutant claims (C76-C79) evaluated separately by OpenEval in R5.

Partial overlap on mechanistic interpretation (C92, C95). OpenEval R5 addresses these as part of CRT mutant functional evidence with concerns about protein integrity. Peer R7 accepts the dual-mode interaction model (C92, C95-C97) as reasonable interpretation, stating 'the model pushed by the authors is better supported by the data.'

Divergent evaluation types for overall regulatory model (C98). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative mechanistic models requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, endorsing the overall conclusion as 'important study' with 'reasonable conclusions.' OpenEval also addresses C90, C97 as untested speculation.

Partial agreement on screen findings (C2, C52-C53). Both support CRT identification from the screen. OpenEval R1 covers extensive validation data (C3-C5, C54-C60) demonstrating constitutive ATF6α activation and specificity. Peer R1 focuses on screen validity and initial identification (C2, C45, C51-C53), praising 'innovative experimental design.'

Minimal overlap on mechanistic model claim C97. OpenEval rates speculative models as UNCERTAIN, requiring validation. Peer R7 accepts dual-mode interaction model including C97 as well-supported interpretation. Different scope: OpenEval R10 addresses titration model speculation, peer R7 addresses broader mechanistic interpretation.

Minimal overlap on screen claim C45. OpenEval R7 focuses on FURIN validation and indirect mechanism. Peer R1 addresses overall screen validity including FURIN as secondary hit. Both support the screen findings but with different emphases.

Peer reviewers evaluated extensive background and literature context claims (C1, C11-C36, C85, C89-C91, C93) as SUPPORTED, treating them as accurate representations of established knowledge. OpenEval did not produce a separate evaluation for these background claims, though C90 appears in OpenEval R10 as part of speculative mechanistic discussion.
